c.tagline: Where the Zambezi thunders into mist and rainbows.

taxi.fareNote: Negotiate or confirm the fare before departure; typical in-town trip $5-8, airport-town run $25-30.

emergency.medical: 994 (ambulance); private evacuation via Medical Air Rescue Service (MARS)
emergency.note: Response times can be slow; most hotels and tour operators keep direct lines to private clinics and MARS for serious incidents.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Zambezi Riverfront: Elephant Hills Resort Golf Course, Victoria Falls

avoid.reason: Expect persistent curio vendors and money-change hustlers in town, and never walk unlit roads at night — elephants, buffalo and hippos roam freely.

hoods: Zambezi National Park / Safari Lodge Estate
hood_desc: The compact tourist core right by the Falls entrance, packed with curio markets, restaurants and bars - best for first-timers who want everything walkable.
A quieter residential pocket a few blocks from the main strip, popular with backpackers and independent travelers wanting value without losing convenience.
Leafy riverside hotels and a golf estate along the Zambezi upstream of the Falls, suited to travelers wanting resort comforts and sunset-cruise access nearby.
Elevated bushveld lodges bordering Zambezi National Park with waterhole views and resident wildlife, ideal for safari-focused travelers near the airport road.
The local township adjoining downtown, offering budget guesthouses, campsites and homestays for travelers wanting a slower, community-based stay.

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water; most lodges provide safe drinking water for guests.

sys.n: National Railways of Zimbabwe (Bulawayo-Victoria Falls line)

transit.pay: Kombi and local taxi fares are paid in cash (USD) directly to the driver; there is no rechargeable card or app-based fare system. Most visitors instead arrange point-to-point transport through hotel front desks, tour operators, or pre-booked shuttle/taxi services.
transit.hours: Kombis and taxis run roughly 6am-9pm with no scheduled night service; hotels arrange private drivers after dark.
transit.note: The town centre is highly walkable, but riverfront hotels, safari lodges and the airport all require taxi, shuttle or hotel transfer.

train: National Railways of Zimbabwe overnight service (Bulawayo-Victoria Falls, a few times weekly)
bus: Intercity coaches to Bulawayo and Harare (operators such as City Link, Pathfinder)

tip.r: 10% at restaurants when service isn't included; $10-20/day for safari guides, $1-2 per bag for porters.

food.name: Sadza with game meat
food.desc: Stiff white maize porridge eaten by hand with relish - here often kudu, impala or warthog stew alongside greens and peanut sauce.

places.name: Mama Africa Eating House
places.note: Long-standing local kitchen mixing Zimbabwean and pan-African dishes, with live jazz on Africa Nights.

places.name: Dusty Road
places.note: Traditional Zimbabwean feast in a quirky yard setting; widely praised as the most authentic meal in town.

places.name: The Boma - Dinner and Drum Show
places.note: Buffet of game meats and traditional sides with drumming and dancing; book ahead.

food.name: Nyama choma braai
food.desc: Meat grilled slowly over charcoal - beef, goat, chicken or game - carved at the fire and eaten with sadza and chilli relish.

places.name: The Boma - Dinner and Drum Show
places.note: Open-fire carvery covering crocodile, warthog and eland as well as the everyday cuts.

places.name: Dusty Road
places.note: Cooks over open fire in an outdoor setting run by locals.

places.name: Mama Africa Eating House
places.note: Grilled meats with African sides in the middle of town, walkable from most hotels.

food.name: Kapenta
food.desc: Tiny dried sardines from Lake Kariba, fried crisp with tomato and onion and served over sadza; salty, intense and thoroughly Zimbabwean.

places.name: Dusty Road
places.note: Serves kapenta as part of its traditional Zimbabwean spread with sadza and greens.

places.name: Mama Africa Eating House
places.note: One of the few in-town restaurants to keep proper kapenta on the menu.

places.name: The Boma
places.note: Buffet includes kapenta and other traditional relishes beside the grilled meats.

food.name: Biltong
food.desc: Air-dried, coriander-spiced strips of beef or game, sliced thin; the road-trip and safari snack of southern Africa.

places.name: Elephant's Walk Shopping Village
places.note: Craft and food shops here sell packaged biltong and droewors to take on game drives.

places.name: The Boma
places.note: Biltong appears among the starters alongside mopane worms for the brave.

places.name: Chinotimba butcheries
places.note: Local butchers cut and dry their own; cheapest and freshest, if you can bargain in bulk.

food.name: Zambezi bream
food.desc: Freshwater tilapia from the Zambezi, grilled whole or filleted with lemon and butter; the river fish that shows up on every menu.

places.name: MaKuwa-Kuwa Restaurant
places.note: First-floor dining room over a floodlit waterhole; menu leans on game meat and local fish.

places.name: The Palm Restaurant
places.note: Closest hotel restaurant to the falls, with the spray visible from the terrace at dinner.

places.name: Lookout Cafe
places.note: Clifftop terrace over the gorge; worth going for the view as much as the food.

food.name: High tea at the Victoria Falls Hotel
food.desc: Colonial-era ritual on a terrace facing the gorge and the bridge: tiered stands of sandwiches, scones and cakes with the falls' spray in view.

places.name: Stanley's Terrace
places.area: The Victoria Falls Hotel, Mallett Drive
places.note: The classic afternoon-tea setting since 1904, looking straight down the gorge to the bridge.

places.name: The Palm Restaurant
places.note: Alternative afternoon tea and cakes closer to the falls entrance, less formal.

food.name: Zambezi Lager
food.desc: Zimbabwe's crisp pale lager, brewed in Harare and drunk ice-cold at sundown; the default sundowner along the river.

places.name: Stanley's Terrace
places.note: Sundowner spot of choice, with the bridge and rising spray in front of you.

places.name: Lookout Cafe
places.note: Cold beer on a terrace hanging over the gorge, often with bungee jumpers below.

places.name: Mama Africa Eating House
places.note: Cheaper in-town pint with music, popular with guides and residents.

food.name: Maheu
food.desc: Traditional non-alcoholic maize drink, lightly fermented and slightly sour, sold chilled in cartons and drunk as much for food as for thirst.

places.name: Chinotimba Market
places.note: Township shops and market stalls sell maheu and traditional sour porridge at local prices.

places.name: Dusty Road
places.note: Offers traditional drinks alongside the Zimbabwean food spread.

landmarks: Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya)
Known locally as 'The Smoke That Thunders', this colossal curtain of water plunging into the Zambezi Gorge is one of the world's most spectacular natural wonders.
Victoria Falls Bridge
This dramatic steel arch bridge spanning the Zambezi Gorge links Zimbabwe and Zambia and is famous worldwide for its bungee jumping and gorge swing.
Devil's Pool
A thrilling natural infinity pool perched right at the lip of the falls lets daring swimmers peer over the precipice during the dry season.
Knife-Edge Bridge
This narrow footbridge drenched in spray offers an exhilarating, up-close view into the churning gorge and the Eastern Cataract of the falls.
David Livingstone Statue
This bronze monument honors the Scottish explorer who named the falls after Queen Victoria and remains a popular photo stop near the main viewpoints.
Zambezi River White-Water Rafting
The turbulent rapids of Batoka Gorge below the falls rank among the world's most thrilling white-water rafting runs, drawing adventure seekers globally.
The Big Tree
This colossal, centuries-old baobab near the falls is a beloved natural landmark and a favorite gathering spot for visitors exploring the area.
Lunar Rainbow (Moonbow) at Victoria Falls
On clear full-moon nights, the spray from the falls creates a rare and magical moonbow, a phenomenon found in only a handful of places worldwide.
Zambezi Sunset Cruise
Gliding along the Zambezi River as the sun sets, with hippos and elephants often visible on the banks, is a quintessential Victoria Falls experience.
Zimbabwe-Side Falls Viewpoints
The Zimbabwean rainforest trail offers the widest and most panoramic vantage points of the falls, drenched in mist and framed by lush vegetation.

train.note: No scheduled cross-border train crosses the Victoria Falls Bridge to Livingstone, Zambia anymore (you can walk across on foot). Domestically, NRZ runs a scenic overnight sleeper to Bulawayo about once a week (currently Sundays, departing ~19:00, arriving ~10:00). Buy tickets in cash in person at Victoria Falls station; there is no online booking. A separate tourist steam excursion on the bridge exists but is not scheduled transport.

bus.note: There is no reliable scheduled international coach directly from Victoria Falls town. Long-distance domestic coaches run to Bulawayo and Harare with City Link (https://www.citylinkcoaches.co.zw/) and Extra City (https://www.extracity.co.zw/); from Bulawayo, Intercape/Pathfinder (https://www.intercape.co.za/) continues to Johannesburg, South Africa. Cross-border trips to Kasane (Botswana) and Livingstone (Zambia) are normally done by private shuttle/transfer rather than a scheduled bus; carry your passport.

ferry.note: Victoria Falls town is not a ferry port and there is no international passenger ferry here. The old Kazungula ferry between Botswana and Zambia was replaced by the Kazungula Bridge in 2021. Zambezi sunset river cruises (e.g. Shearwater, Wild Horizons) are scenic excursions only, not transport.

half.name: Livingstone
half.blurb: Livingstone is a Zambian town across the border with its own viewpoint of the falls and the Livingstone Museum.

full.name: Chobe National Park
full.blurb: Chobe National Park in Botswana is known for large elephant herds along the Chobe River, reached via the Kazungula border crossing.

full.name: Hwange National Park
full.blurb: Hwange National Park is Zimbabwe's largest game reserve, with a wide variety of wildlife around its waterholes.
